newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay extradites embassy threat suspect to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay extradites embassy threat suspect to U.S.

text.p: One of four men arrested suspected of participating in threats against the U.S. Embassy in Asuncion has been extradited to the United States from Paraguay, a police officials said on Saturday.
Police spokesman Miguel Ferreira said agents took the 40-year-old Lebanese national, identified as Marwan Adib Adam Kadi, or Marwan Safarit, to New York late on Friday.
"The detainee was handed over to special U.S. agents because he is suspected of having participated in attacks in other countries," Ferreira told Reuters. He said Kadi was arrested on Thursday.
Two other Lebanese nationals arrested in the border town of Ciudad del Este in connection with threats to the American Embassy this week have since been released, police said.

A fourth man arrested in the case, a retired Paraguayan army colonel, was being held on suspicion of handing over forged documents to illegal aliens, but his case was being handled by military courts that traditionally provide little public information on their proceedings.
The U.S. Embassy declined immediate comment on the reports and an "official version on the case" will not be available until Tuesday, embassy spokesman James Dickmeyer said.
U.S. diplomats said on Tuesday the American Embassy was threatened by an international guerrilla group that officials in Washington hinted could be the Iranian-backed Hizbollah.

The embassy suspended public celebrations of the U.S. presidential election after receiving what it termed a "terrorist threat." A statement on the threat was also issued by the U.S. State Department in Washington.

Asked if Hizbollah, which is best known in Lebanon but also reportedly has affiliates in other countries, was behind the threat, a U.S. official said on Tuesday: "I wouldn't steer you away from that."
Another official said: "I don't think we're talking about indigenous groups here. We're talking about groups that operate on a global basis."

The Moslem fundamentalist Hizbollah has been blamed for past attacks in neighbouring Argentina that destroyed the Israeli Embassy in Buenos Aires in 1992, killing 29 people, and a Jewish community centre there in 1994, killing 86.

U.S. experts on Latin America have suggested guerrillas might choose Paraguay for an attack because of the relative ease of fleeing the country, especially from Ciudad del Este, where the borders of Paraguay, Argentina and Brazil meet.
